symptom: An `if` without `else` inside a custom error handler (`on error without rollback begin if $Flag then return 1; end if; return -1; end error;`), whose THEN ends in RETURN, passed check and exec, but the decision's second outgoing flow was stored with NoCase instead of `false`: mx check reported CE0079 "The 'false' condition value should be configured…" at the decision and CE0773 "Value must be of type Boolean." at the flow. describe read the NoCase edge back as an `else`. The same `if` in the main flow, with an explicit else, or with a THEN that does not return was stored correctly (ako/mxcli#1455, mendixlabs/mxcli#1558)
cause: Such an `if` has no merge, so addIfStatement leaves its FALSE edge pending in nextConnectionPoint/nextFlowCase/nextFlowAnchor for the NEXT flow to carry. addErrorHandlerFlow's handler-body loop copied the case into lastErrCase but used it only for takePendingJoin and the handler's final rejoin; the edge to the next statement inside the handler was drawn with a plain newHorizontalFlow, dropping the case — and the deferred @anchor(false: …) with it. Every other body loop (top level, IF arms, CASE/type-split arms, loop/while bodies) takes both
insight: When one body loop misbehaves and the same construct is fine elsewhere, grep every `newHorizontalFlow(last…ID, actID)` and check each sits in the else of a pending-case test: here all seven siblings did and the handler loop alone did not, which localised it in one step. Carry the deferred anchor too (pendingFlowAnchors when the previous statement was compound) — a test reverting only the anchor half fails 1→3 vs bottom→top, so it is a separate, real omission. Assert on the edges' cases, not describe text: describe renders the NoCase edge as an `else`, which reads correct and even round-trips (re-exec of the describe output builds a valid if/else), hiding the defect. Distinct from ako/mxcli#1459 (fall-through handlers inside branches), same cluster
